name: Trowel-Basin

civilization.name: The Shapers
civilization.notes: A civilization of master builders who construct vast adobe cities in canyon walls using a mortar mixed from desert minerals and their own biochemical secretions. They practice a form of geological worship.

description: Trowel-Basin is a world of warm ochre deserts and immense canyon systems that cut through layered sedimentary rock like the marks of some planetary mason's tool. The canyon walls display billions of years of geological history in bands of red, gold, and cream, and it is into these walls that the Shapers have carved their magnificent cities. Dust seas fill the basins between canyon networks, their surfaces rippled by constant winds into patterns that shift daily but somehow always return to the same fundamental forms.

The breathable atmosphere is dry and dust-laden, tinting the sky a permanent amber and creating sunsets of extraordinary chromatic range. The canyon interiors trap cooler air and channel breezes that make the Shaper cities surprisingly comfortable, their adobe walls releasing stored heat slowly through the cold desert nights. The sound of the canyons is the sound of wind through carved stone, a deep, fluting resonance that the Shapers incorporate into their architectural designs as a form of worship.

The Shapers appear to have built their civilization atop much older ruins, foundations and buried chambers that extend far deeper into the canyon walls than their own construction. These ancient structures use a different building material and a radically different architectural philosophy, suggesting a predecessor civilization that vanished long before the Shapers emerged. The Shapers call these deep places the Roots of the World and incorporate them into their cosmology as the work of divine builders.

A quarantine zone protects the Shapers from external contact, but their canyon cities are growing rapidly, and new construction is beginning to uncover more of the ancient ruins. The predecessor civilization's building material has proven to be a room-temperature superconductor of extraordinary efficiency, a discovery with enormous technological implications. The ethical tension between protecting the Shapers and accessing the ruins beneath their cities has created a political crisis that shows no sign of resolution.
